from.place: Proof paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint (current main-20261015 path sk-thm-sf-package), coherent derived coefficient adjunction before the displayed derived-limit calculation; auxiliary accessible small-object construction for the model-localization infrastructure.

title: Accessible small-object factorizations
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with small Hom sets and small colimits as in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], in a fixed universe. A category is locally presentable if it is cocomplete and, for some infinite regular cardinal $\kappa$, generated under small $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small set of objects $P$ such that $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ preserves these colimits. Here $\kappa$-filtered means every diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms admits a cocone, and regular means a union of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of cardinality less than $\kappa$ has cardinality less than $\kappa$. Suppose $\mathcal C$ is locally presentable, and let $I$ be a small set of its morphisms. Use diagonal lifting and arrow retracts as in [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. A weakly saturated class contains isomorphisms and is closed under pushouts, small transfinite compositions, and retracts in the arrow category; a small transfinite composition is the map from the first object to the colimit of an ordinal-indexed sequence continuous at limit ordinals. There is a functorial factorization $f=p_f i_f$ of every arrow $f:X\to Y$ with $i_f$ in the weakly saturated class generated by $I$ and $p_f$ having the right lifting property against $I$. Its middle-object functor $E:\mathcal C^{[1]}\to\mathcal C$ can be chosen to preserve small $\kappa$-filtered colimits for some infinite regular $\kappa$. Here $\mathcal C^{[1]}$ is the category of arrows and commuting squares, with colimits computed on source and target; functorial means that a commuting square $(a,b):f\to g$ induces $E(a,b)$ with $E(a,b)i_f=i_ga$ and $p_gE(a,b)=bp_f$, compatibly with identities and composition.

source.place: Proposition A.1.2.5(1)-(2), printed pp. 790-791 (PDF pp. 807-808). The preservation of sufficiently filtered colimits is additional to mere existence of functorial factorization. No Stacks tag states the accessible small-object theorem. Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Write the generating maps as $i:A_i\to B_i$, $i\in I$, and denote the fixed universe by $\mathcal U$. Apply [lem-coef-object-presentability-rank] separately to every $A_i$ and $B_i$. Obtain infinite regular ranks $\tau_{i,0},\tau_{i,1}\in\mathcal U$ for which their respective Hom functors preserve all small filtered colimits of those ranks. Its assumptions are precisely the local presentability, Hom-smallness and cocompleteness of this item. Both ends are needed below; smallness of the domains alone would not prove accessibility of the attaching-square functor.

source.place: Lines 93-101; HTT Proposition A.1.2.5(2), selection of compactness bounds for both ends.

proof.text: For each $(i,e)\in I\times\{0,1\}$ take the set of ordinals below the initial ordinal of cardinality $\tau_{i,e}$. Their disjoint union $T$ is $\mathcal U$-small. Apply [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] to this family to choose an infinite regular $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ with $|T|<\kappa$. The inclusion of each summand gives $\tau_{i,e}\leq |T|<\kappa$. This also works for $I=\varnothing$. Fix this one cardinal for the entire construction, independently of the arrow being factored.

source.place: Lines 199-206, applied to the small family of both endpoint ranks.

proof.text: Every $\kappa$-filtered category is $\tau_{i,e}$-filtered, simply because a diagram with fewer than $\tau_{i,e}$ morphisms has fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms. Thus both endpoint Hom functors preserve small $\kappa$-filtered colimits. The ordinal category $\{\alpha:\alpha<\kappa\}$ is itself $\kappa$-filtered: the images of a diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms have fewer than $\kappa$ objects, hence form fewer than $\kappa$ ordinals below $\kappa$; their supremum is below $\kappa$ by regularity and provides a cocone. For an empty diagram use $0$. The infinite initial ordinal $\kappa$ is a nonzero limit, since $\alpha+1<\kappa$ for every $\alpha<\kappa$. All these ordinal categories are small in $\mathcal U$.

source.place: Proposition A.1.2.5 proof, regular ordinal used for iteration; details of filteredness supplied from the definitions.

proof.text: For an arrow $q:V\to Y$ define the small set $Q_i(q)=\{(a,b):a:A_i\to V,\ b:B_i\to Y,\ qa=bi\}$, and let $Q(q)=\coprod_{i\in I}Q_i(q)$. It is small because each $Q_i(q)$ is a subset of the product of two small Hom sets and $I$ is small. For a commuting square $(c,d):q\to q'$ the formula $(a,b)\mapsto(ca,db)$ gives a function $Q_i(q)\to Q_i(q')$: indeed $q'ca=dqa=dbi$. The formulas preserve identities and composites. Thus each $Q_i$ and their disjoint union are genuine functors on the arrow category.

source.place: Proposition A.1.2.5 proof, functors F_i; their extension to varying targets is written explicitly.

proof.text: Choose the coproducts $A(q)=\coprod_{(i,a,b)\in Q(q)}A_i$ and $B(q)=\coprod_{(i,a,b)\in Q(q)}B_i$. Their summands give maps $A(q)\to V$, $A(q)\to B(q)$ and $B(q)\to Y$ with commuting composite to $Y$. Form the pushout $S(q)=V\amalg_{A(q)}B(q)$. By [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], applied to small discrete and span diagrams, these objects exist and the compatible maps to $Y$ induce $q^+:S(q)\to Y$. If $c_q:V\to S(q)$ is the pushout leg, then $q^+c_q=q$. For every attaching triple the other leg gives $d_{i,a,b}:B_i\to S(q)$ satisfying $d_{i,a,b}i=c_qa$ and $q^+d_{i,a,b}=b$.

source.place: Proposition A.1.2.5 proof, displayed successor pushout; Stacks Tags 002D, 002F for its universal property.

proof.text: For a square $(c,d):q\to q'$, the function on triples in step 4 gives coproduct maps $A(q)\to A(q')$ and $B(q)\to B(q')$, using the identity on each corresponding $A_i$ or $B_i$. Together with $c$ these induce the unique $S(c,d):S(q)\to S(q')$ satisfying $S(c,d)c_q=c_{q'}c$ and carrying the summand map of $(i,a,b)$ to that of $(i,ca,db)$. Equality after the two pushout legs proves $q'^+S(c,d)=dq^+$. The same uniqueness proves identity and composition laws. Hence $q\mapsto q^+$ is an endofunctor of the arrow category and $c_q$ is natural; its middle-object functor is $S$.

source.place: Proposition A.1.2.5 proof, functoriality of successor pushouts, expanded via Stacks Tag 002F.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-transfinite-recursion] on $\{\beta:\beta\leq\kappa\}$, for each input $f:X\to Y$. The stage records consist of $Z_\beta$, $p_\beta:Z_\beta\to Y$ and maps $u_{\alpha\beta}:Z_\alpha\to Z_\beta$ with invariant $u_{\alpha\alpha}=1$, $u_{\beta\gamma}u_{\alpha\beta}=u_{\alpha\gamma}$ and $p_\beta u_{\alpha\beta}=p_\alpha$. At zero use $Z_0=X$, $p_0=f$. At a successor use $Z_{\alpha+1}=S(p_\alpha)$, $p_{\alpha+1}=p_\alpha^+$, $u_{\alpha,\alpha+1}=c_{p_\alpha}$, and $u_{\delta,\alpha+1}=c_{p_\alpha}u_{\delta\alpha}$. At a nonzero limit $\beta$ take $Z_\beta=\varinjlim_{\alpha<\beta}Z_\alpha$, its cocone maps as transitions, and the induced map $p_\beta$ to $Y$, using [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The successor identities follow from $p_\alpha^+c_{p_\alpha}=p_\alpha$ and the previous invariant; at limits they are the cocone and induced-map equations. Thus the invariant holds at every stage. To make the recursion rule total on arbitrary prefixes of records, include a dummy record and return it on any incoherent prefix; the displayed checks prove by induction that it never occurs. Every required diagram has small index, since $\beta\leq\kappa\in\mathcal U$.

source.place: Proposition A.1.2.5 proof, transfinite chain; recursion leaf has Stacks provenance Tag 03C3 and Mathlib Order/RelClasses.lean:304-313.

proof.text: A square $(a,b):f\to g$ induces maps $m_\beta:Z_\beta(f)\to Z_\beta(g)$ by the same recursion: $m_0=a$, $m_{\alpha+1}=S(m_\alpha,b)$, and at a nonzero limit $m_\beta$ is induced by the compatible maps $u_{\alpha\beta}(g)m_\alpha$. The induction invariant is $m_\beta u_{\alpha\beta}(f)=u_{\alpha\beta}(g)m_\alpha$ and $p_\beta(g)m_\beta=bp_\beta(f)$. Step 6 proves the successor case; the cocone equations prove the limit case. For an identity square these maps are identities by induction and uniqueness at limits. For composable squares the maps are the composites by step 6 at successors and the same uniqueness at limits. This verifies functoriality and natural transition maps, rather than choosing unrelated factorizations of individual arrows.

source.place: Proposition A.1.2.5 proof, functorial transfinite construction; successor and limit equations expanded.

proof.text: Set $E(f)=Z_\kappa(f)$, $i_f=u_{0\kappa}$, $p_f=p_\kappa$. The invariant gives $p_fi_f=f$. Put $E(a,b)=m_\kappa$; step 8 gives a functor and the equations $E(a,b)i_f=i_ga$ and $p_gE(a,b)=bp_f$. Its chain is continuous at nonzero limits, and every successor is a pushout of the small coproduct indexed by $Q(p_\alpha)$. It remains to check membership in the specified weak saturation, right lifting, and preservation of filtered colimits for this very construction.

source.place: Proposition A.1.2.5(1)-(2), defining the final factorization from the continuous chain.

proof.text: Let $W$ be any weakly saturated class containing $I$. For any successor pushout $V\to V\amalg_{\coprod_t A_{i_t}}\coprod_t B_{i_t}$, well-order its small attaching set by [lem-weil-pbc-well-ordering-theorem], and identify its order type with a small ordinal $\theta$. For $\beta\leq\theta$ put $V_\beta=V\amalg_{\coprod_{t<\beta}A_{i_t}}\coprod_{t<\beta}B_{i_t}$, using the original attaching maps to $V$. Then $V_0\cong V$, each $V_\beta\to V_{\beta+1}$ is a pushout of $i_\beta$, and at a nonzero limit $\delta$ the maps $V_\beta\to V_\delta$ exhibit the colimit: a compatible family of maps out is exactly a map from $V$ and maps from $B_{i_t}$ for $t<\delta$ agreeing on each $A_{i_t}$. These assertions follow from [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and also identify $V_\theta$ with the original simultaneous pushout. Thus that successor belongs to $W$ by pushout and transfinite-composition closure. The empty attaching set gives an isomorphism, also in $W$. Apply transfinite-composition closure once more to the continuous $\kappa$-chain of step 7: $i_f\in W$. Since $W$ was arbitrary, $i_f$ belongs to the weakly saturated class generated by $I$. No closure under coproducts was assumed without justification.

source.place: Proposition A.1.2.5(1) and Definition A.1.2.2; explicit serialization of simultaneous attachments. Well-ordering leaf has Stacks provenance Tag 065T.

proof.text: For right lifting, fix $i:A_i\to B_i$ in $I$ and a square $p_fa=bi$ with $a:A_i\to Z_\kappa$ and $b:B_i\to Y$. By step 3, $\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,-)$ preserves the colimit of the small filtered ordinal chain $\alpha<\kappa$. Hence its colimit is $\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,Z_\kappa)$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] to $a$, obtaining $\alpha<\kappa$ and $a_\alpha:A_i\to Z_\alpha$ with $u_{\alpha\kappa}a_\alpha=a$. The invariant gives $p_\alpha a_\alpha=p_fu_{\alpha\kappa}a_\alpha=p_fa=bi$, so $(i,a_\alpha,b)$ is an actual attaching triple at stage $\alpha$. No factorization of $b$ or eventual-equality assertion is needed, since the target remains $Y$.

source.place: Tag 04AX, section-directed-colimits, the quotient description after Definition 002V; applied to the preserved Hom colimit.

proof.text: The summand map $d:B_i\to Z_{\alpha+1}$ of step 5 satisfies $di=u_{\alpha,\alpha+1}a_\alpha$ and $p_{\alpha+1}d=b$. Since $\alpha+1<\kappa$, set $h=u_{\alpha+1,\kappa}d$. The transition identities give $hi=u_{\alpha\kappa}a_\alpha=a$ and $p_fh=p_{\alpha+1}d=b$. Thus $p_f$ has the right lifting property against every member of $I$.

source.place: Proposition A.1.2.5(1), explicit next-stage filler and passage to the final chain.

proof.text: Now let $J$ be any small $\kappa$-filtered category and let $(q_j:V_j\to Y_j)_{j\in J}$ be a diagram of arrows. Write $V=\varinjlim_j V_j$, $Y=\varinjlim_j Y_j$, and let $q:V\to Y$ be the induced arrow; these endpoint colimits form the colimit of the arrow diagram. For each $i$ there is a natural equality $Q_i(q)=\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,V)\times_{\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,Y)}\operatorname{Hom}(B_i,Y)$, where the two maps are composition with $q$ and precomposition with $i$. All three Hom functors preserve the $J$-colimits by step 3, and $J$ is filtered because $\kappa$ is infinite. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits] to this fibre-product diagram of sets. It gives the canonical bijection $\varinjlim_j Q_i(q_j)\cong Q_i(q)$, natural in $i$ and the input diagram. This is precisely where presentability of the codomains $B_i$ is used.

source.place: Tag 002W, lemma-directed-commutes, applied to the finite pullback-shaped category.

proof.text: For a fixed object $D$, write $T\odot D=\coprod_{t\in T}D$ for a small set $T$. Its coproduct universal property gives $\operatorname{Hom}(T\odot D,H)=\operatorname{Map}(T,\operatorname{Hom}(D,H))$. If $T$ is a colimit of sets $T_j$, maps from $T$ into this last set are exactly compatible maps from $T_j$; thus $\varinjlim_j(T_j\odot D)\cong T\odot D$, with the canonical summand maps. Apply this to $D=A_i,B_i$ and the bijections in step 13. Interchange the small coproduct over $i$ and the colimit over $j$ using [lem-pc-colimit-fubini], with its second index the discrete category on $I$. Consequently the canonical maps $\varinjlim_j A(q_j)\to A(q)$ and $\varinjlim_j B(q_j)\to B(q)$ are isomorphisms. These identifications also respect the attaching maps, since on a summand $(i,a,b)$ they use exactly $a$, $i$, and $b$.

source.place: Tags 002F and 002M, lemma-colimits-commute, with a discrete small index; copower preservation proved from its universal property.

proof.text: The three vertices of the pushout span $V_j\leftarrow A(q_j)\to B(q_j)$ have $J$-colimits $V\leftarrow A(q)\to B(q)$ by steps 13-14 and the source colimit. Use [lem-pc-colimit-fubini] with the finite span category to interchange this pushout and $\varinjlim_j$. It identifies $\varinjlim_j S(q_j)$ with $S(q)$ by the canonical map, so the one-step middle-object functor $S$ preserves every small $\kappa$-filtered colimit. The maps to $Y$ agree under this identification, because on $V_j$ and every attaching summand both composites are their specified maps to $Y$. Hence the arrow-valued one-step functor $q\mapsto q^+$ also preserves these colimits. No preservation of finite limits in $\mathcal C$ has been used; only the finite limit of sets in step 13 is involved.

source.place: Tag 002M, lemma-colimits-commute, with the pushout-shaped finite category.

proof.text: For every $\beta\leq\kappa$, prove by transfinite induction that $f\mapsto Z_\beta(f)$ preserves small $\kappa$-filtered colimits. At $0$ it is source evaluation, which preserves them since arrow colimits are computed on endpoints. If it holds at $\alpha$, then $f\mapsto p_\alpha(f):Z_\alpha(f)\to\operatorname{cod}(f)$ preserves them as an arrow-valued functor: both endpoint comparisons are isomorphisms and the comparison square commutes by naturality in step 8. Compose this with $S$, whose preservation was proved in step 15, to obtain the successor assertion. At a nonzero limit $\beta$, step 8 makes $(\alpha,j)\mapsto Z_\alpha(f_j)$ a genuine diagram on $(\alpha<\beta)\times J$. Each $\alpha$-stage comparison is an isomorphism by induction. Apply [lem-pc-colimit-fubini] to get $\varinjlim_j Z_\beta(f_j)\cong\varinjlim_{\alpha<\beta}\varinjlim_j Z_\alpha(f_j)\cong\varinjlim_{\alpha<\beta}Z_\alpha(\varinjlim_j f_j)=Z_\beta(\varinjlim_j f_j)$. All comparisons are canonical and hence commute with the transition maps. Both index categories are small; no bound $\beta<\kappa$ is needed for colimits to commute. In particular the assertion at $\beta=\kappa$ says that $E$ preserves the required colimits, completing all clauses of the item.

source.place: Tag 002M, lemma-colimits-commute, used at limit stages of the explicit transfinite induction; HTT Proposition A.1.2.5(2).

HTT is not archived, so I checked the statement against the proposition from memory: presentable C, small I, weak saturation, right lifting against I, functoriality and kappa-filtered accessibility all agree. I read the statements of all 9 cited nodes. All 8 proof dependencies are Mathlib leaves (object rank LocallyPresentable.lean:93-101, regular bound HasCardinalLT.lean:199-206, transfinite recursion, well-ordering, filtered colimits of sets elementwise, filtered colimits commuting with finite limits Stacks 002W, Fubini 002M), and each says what its step takes. Step checks: both endpoint ranks are bounded below one regular kappa, including I empty; kappa-filtered implies tau-filtered; the ordinal kappa is kappa-filtered; the square and attaching-set functors satisfy qa=bi; pushout maps come from uniqueness; the recursion invariants cover zero, successor and limit; maps on squares are functorial; simultaneous attachments are serialized as pushouts of single generators, so i_f is in every weakly saturated W containing I without assuming coproduct closure; the lift uses a_alpha with the target Y fixed and h=u_{alpha+1,kappa}d; Q_i is a fibre product of Hom sets that commutes with filtered colimits (this needs the codomain ranks); copower, coproduct and pushout comparisons use Fubini; the final induction preserves colimits at 0, successors and limits. Steps 3, 4, 9 and 12 are genuinely elementary. Small cases tested: I empty, an empty attaching set, initial domains, identity generators, terminal C. There are no new nodes. The near candidates (cardinal, cell, presentable and presentable-cellular small-object factorization nodes) lack the accessibility clause, so there is no duplicate. No tool_uses are needed and nothing comes from SGA. The unit is unchanged; from.place names paragraph 2 of the main-20261015 proof of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint, which I read. lean.statement: theorem exists_accessible_functorial_factorization {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasColimitsOfSize.{v, v} C] [IsLocallyPresentable.{v} C] (I : MorphismProperty C) [IsSmall.{v} I] : ∃ (κ : Cardinal.{v}) (_ : Fact κ.IsRegular) (data : I.rlp.llp.FunctorialFactorizationData I.rlp), data.Z.IsCardinalAccessible κ ∧ ∀ P : MorphismProperty C, I ≤ P → isomorphisms C ≤ P → P.IsStableUnderCobaseChange → P.IsStableUnderTransfiniteComposition.{v} → P.IsStableUnderRetracts → ∀ f : Arrow C, P (data.i.app f)
